evidence: Every matrix differs densely (Adam). OV maps are unchanged; the structured difference is in QK. In layers 6-17 copy heads (positive OV eigenvalues) and copy-suppression heads (negative) received strongly anti-aligned query changes (cos up to -0.72, z up to -24) on one key feature shared across layers 8-17: a rebalancing of copying versus suppressing one in-context token (the user's guess). Orientation-free RoPE kernels (q_norm-projected) show that, relative to the template tokens, A's suppressors and B's copy heads gained attention on content positions (70-80% and 61-67% of heads), and B's MLPs have a higher token-copy trace (z~+3.3, robust to null and weighting), so B copies the guess and A suppresses it. Caveat: if the correct answer were listed as an option before the guess, the call could flip; per-head norm and rescale statistics were Adam artifacts and were discarded.
